steps.text: Stir sugar, milk, and butter in a saucepan over medium heat; bring to a boil. Cook at a rolling boil for 30 seconds, then immediately remove from the heat.
Add chocolate chips and vanilla to the saucepan; stir until chocolate chips are completely melted. Pour immediately over warm brownies.

raw_recipe.headline: Brownie Frosting
raw_recipe.description: This chocolate frosting for brownies makes any batch of treats even sweeter. This 5-ingredient icing recipe works on homemade and boxed brownies.
raw_recipe.name: Brownie Frosting

review.reviewBody: This is a thick, glossy, fudge-like frosting, perfect, I agree, for brownies, though I used it to frost My Mom's Chocolate Cake, also from this site. I prepared this exactly as written and found both the ingredients and the directions to be spot on. Hubs called this frosting a cross between a truffle and fudge. I just call it darn good!

I submitted this recipe and I cannot stress enough how you need to make sure it is boiling properly and for the time specified. Also, the frosting won't separate from the brownie if you put it on when the brownies are still warm. My habit with making this is to put all the ingredients into the pot that need to boil together while the brownies bake. I also put the cup of chocolate chips in the measuring cup and add the splash of vanilla (otherwise I forget it) to that cup. As soon as I mix in the chocolate chips, I pour it over the brownies. I never have problems with separation. It amazes me the ways people have used this frosting and the variations they have found work for them. I can honestly say it never occurred to me to use this on anything other than brownies, and my Mom was equally shocked when I told her people use it on other things! Thanks for giving ME ideas for ways to use this. I do have a friend who refers to the brownies I make with this frosting as "brudge" -- a combination of brownie and fudge. ;-)

I made this for my family and they loved it. But I did make some changes because of some of the ratings I read. I used evaporated milk instead of milk, hoping this would help to ensure they frosting was not too thin and runny. It worked perfectly. Plus, I think it made it more creamy and fudge like. I also started out cooking Sugar, Evaporated Milk and Butter on very low heat until mixture was smooth and fully combined. Then I raised heat and brought to a boil. Boiled for 30 sec. like recipe called for. It is very sweet but ITS FROSTING FOR BROWNIES! Just grab a glass of milk. lol.

THE BEST CHOCOLATE FROSTING EVER EVER! I make it in the microwave. I melt the butter about a minute. Then add the milk (I like to use evaporated milk), vanilla, and sugar (I used Splenda.) Stir it up really well & microwave about 90 seconds or less, until it gets frothy. Then I add the chocolate chips and mix it thoroughly with a fork. That's it with only a bowl to clean.

Thank you so much for this masterpiece!

Unbelievable.......I mean UNBELIEVABLE! Made for my friend who is addicted to chocolate so I made “ 20 servings “recipe. Which wasn’t necessary, regular serving would have been plenty. I made box brownies added walnuts & coconut (needed to use coconut extract for more flavor). Used semi-sweet & milk chocolate chips, called for 2.5 cups I used 2 cups of sugar but that could be cut more also. I used Silk soy milk, no problem! I cooked it longer, as brownies weren’t done. If you have a grit feeling, sugar didn’t melt. I cooked on lower temp kept stirring till I couldn’t feel sugar in pan. Anyway, it’s a chocolate lover’s dream, absolutely delish!! Thanks “Crunchm”, great recipe!!!

This recipe is great 👍. I even made it as fudge, and it was delicious. 🍫To use as fudge, follow the original brownie frosting recipe and while it is cooking on the stove, get out a 8 x 8 in. pan out and grease it. Once you have finished the brownie frosting recipe, pour into the 8 x 8“ pan and stick it in the freezer for an hour and a half. Enjoy ☺️ Even feel free to put on your favorite candy toppings as well.

WOW! This stuff is SOOOO good. I halved the recipe for a 8 inch round pan of brownies and it was the perfect amount. I used Ghirardelli 60% cacao bittersweet chocolate chips. I could eat a bowl of this stuff without brownies it was that good. It reminded me of the frosting on Wegman's chocolate cake.

Mixed bag here. Pros: Easy to throw together in just a few minutes. Pretty, glossy finish. Cons: very slightly grainy texture. Too sweet for us. As I had suspected, the chocolate flavor is only as good as the chocolate you use. The first time I make a recipe, I like to give it a fair shake and stay as true to the listed ingredients possible. It calls for "chocolate chips" so that's what I used. And, unfortunately, that's what it tasted like. In the future if I do make this again, I will sub bittersweet chocolate, which I believe will make this so much better in taste, and will have the additional benefit of cutting back on the sweetness. As for the texture, I believe about 30 more seconds of boiling would take care of that. Not bad, but there's room for improvement.

Stumbled upon this recipe looking for something to jazz up some plain boxed brownies since my 7 year old has been trying to learn the basics of baking. OMG, this did it for sure! We made thick brownies in an 8x8 so we thought a thick topping would suit them well so we also made a full batch of frosting. Since this goes on with the brownies still being warm it locks in the moisture resulting in as many have said before me " chocolate crack" that would be perfect with some vanilla icecream, a glass of milk or coffee. Personally I'm thinking Vanilla Gelato with Chocolate Wine. I noticed that several others noted theirs ended up being grainy, this happens with fudge that is not cooked long enough too. Make sure you get a nice rolling boil it should actually start to turn slightly more white in color at this point if you don't you will still have sugar granuals that did not melt which will make for a rather dissapointing frosting. Alternately I you should be able to substitue powdered sugar for the granulated sugar and not need to be as careful in having it boil for the correct duration but you still need to watch closely so you don't over cook/ burn your frosting. This should come out super thick and creamy, so pour it fast before it starts to set in your saucepan. My daughter was helping so we still had quite a bit left in the sauce pan which was fun for the kids once it cooled down enough for them to be able to lick the spoon and pan. Nothing went to waste : ) Pretty sure we w

Super good! Pretty sweet so I add a lot of nuts and use about half the recipe on a single 8x8 pan of brownies. I refrigerated the other half and used it a few days later. To reuse all I did was drop the cold chunk of it right on top of a fresh out of the oven pan of brownies and walked away. When I came back, the heat of the brownies had melted it and it coated the entire pan beautifully. I figured I’d just come back and smooth it out once it softened but I literally didn’t have to do a thing. So nice! On my second make of the frosting I used half brown sugar and it was very good still. Thank you for this recipe!
Yes,this is a wonderful recipe--but too much frosting for 9x13. I halved the recipe--same cooking time, etc. and turned out just fine.
It was great on top of brownies! It kept the brownies super moist. It tasted best at room temperature. I did chill the brownies with frosting overnight, but let them come to room temp the next day.
This frosting is rich and easy to make and tops the brownie perfectly 🌀
I made a tiny adjustment to the recipe by adding a splash (2 tbl) bourbon. Totally optional. Adds a different dimension to the chocolate.

Amazing recipe! The frosting consistency is more like fudge, very thick. Fairly easy to make, and then pour over brownie in tray. After poured I put the brownies + frosting in the refrigerator for the frosting to harden from its melted state. The flavor is very good and chocolatey, it sort of overpowers the brownie, but I don't mind because the frosting tastes great.
I had a hard time getting the chocolate chips to fully melt. It was lumpy. I stirred it for a long time and smashed the chips to help it along, and still lumpy.

This was horribly rich and got rock hard after a day on the brownies. Someone mentioned that they use this recipe as fudge. That’s exactly what it is - fudge. Way too rich to put on brownies!
liked it
This was my grandmother's recipe and has always been a prize winning frosting!
